summary: 6f1da4eb (pass 3's own fix for DW3-1) introduced a new categorical claim that was never seen by any of the 3 Gate 8 agents -- it was written after their reports landed. The clause read: 'for the latter [kCharges], there was nothing pinned to reclaim from in the first place.' Verified false against mcp_stream_bridge.cpp:340-427: `pin_slots_held = unpinned > 0 ? kCharges : kPins` selects kCharges whenever ANY slot on the session is unpinned, regardless of whether OTHER slots on the same session are pinned. A mixed state (e.g. pinned=1, unpinned=3, cap=4) reaches rejection under kCharges; the reclaim attempt (`select_displaceable_pin_locked`, gated only on `pinned + unpinned >= cap`, not on unpinned==0) still runs against the real pinned final and can decline it (the same mid-projection-stall decline branch #2791's tests exercise) -- so in that reachable case, something WAS pinned, the reclaim DID try, it just could not take it. Same defect shape as SCOPE-1 (pass 2) and DW3-1 (pass 3): a per-subcase truth promoted to a per-branch categorical claim, surviving a restructuring that changed the population it describes -- the sixth instance of this branch's recurring pattern, this time introduced BY the fix for the fifth instance.
